situation: Moralis getFilteredTokens was returning unexpected data. Whale accumulation signals were not matching expected timeframes.
root_cause: The timeframe parameter was set to an invalid enum value. Moralis API returns 200 OK with default timeframe data instead of erroring on invalid values — a silent failure.
solution: Added timeframe validation against the documented enum values before making API calls. Logged the actual timeframe used in each request.
lesson: Moralis (and many REST APIs) silently accept invalid enum values and return default data instead of errors. Always validate parameters client-side before making API calls.

user_feedback.comments: Tricky bug — silent API failures are the worst kind
